visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) The video opens in a bright retail space focusing on "Body Cooler" mannequins. A mannequin wears a light olive tank top and black arm sleeves. A hand points to a blue circular "UV Cut" sign attached to the clothing. The environment is a clean, brightly lit department store. (2) Entrance of the "Ito Yokado Food Park ABENO." A woman with her hair in a bun, wearing a black sweatshirt and blue trousers, waves enthusiastically at the camera. The background shows shoppers and the store's red and blue logo. (3) Close-up shots of various cooling garments including tank tops and underwear displayed on hangers. The woman's hands touch a beige bra with a mesh back to demonstrate breathiness. Size charts and price tags in Japanese Yen are shown. (4) A dedicated shelf for insect repellents featuring "Skin Vape" and "Mamo Room" brands. The camera pans across bottles of spray and electronic diffusers. Bright yellow "Value" stickers are visible on the shelving units. (5) Transition to "TOYLO PARK," a colorful entertainment zone. The woman walks through an entrance adorned with neon lights. The area is filled with gashapon (capsule toy) machines and crane games featuring plush characters. (6) Display of novelty stationery, specifically pens topped with realistic sushi, snacks like Calbee, and ramen. The woman holds these up to the camera. Nearby are shelves stacked high with various blind box collectible toys. (7) A section showcasing children's school bags (randoseru) in colors like red, blue, and purple. The camera then moves to Nike-branded athletic wear for children, including black sports bras and blue shorts on display. (8) The cashier counter features a "CASHIER" sign in a vintage circus style with red and white stripes. The woman is seen in a fitting room mirror trying on a black blazer over her casual outfit. (9) The "Found Good" travel section displays a variety of luggage. Multiple suitcases in colors like red, purple, and blue are lined up on shelves. Price tags highlight a large suitcase for 8,800 Yen. (10) Supermarket refrigerated aisles. The woman picks up containers of milk and juice. Rows of Tropicana apple juice and various dairy products are neatly organized under bright white lights. (11) An extensive snack aisle filled with bags of Calbee potato chips. The woman holds up two different packets of chocolate-covered fruit snacks and then two bags of "Kansai style" seasoned chips. (12) Close-ups of Yakult Y1000 bottles, both the classic red and the new light blue version. The woman then presents a box of Haagen-Dazs ice cream bars with macadamia nuts from a freezer. (13) A printed receipt with an "Ito Yokado" logo is held up, specifically pointing out a 20% off discount coupon valid for pharmaceutical and cosmetic products. The background is a store interior. (14) A final exterior view of the Ito Yokado building entrance. The video ends on a pink screen with a large QR code and Traditional Chinese text inviting viewers to scan for details.

The BGM is a mid-tempo acoustic pop track featuring rhythmic acoustic guitar strumming and a clean electronic drum beat. (2) As the speaker describes cooling clothes, the vocal intensity is moderate and clear. There is no audible breathiness or strain. The background music remains constant, providing a cheerful bed. Occasional rustling sounds of clothing hangers are heard as she handles items. (3) The narrator's pitch rises slightly while discussing the toy and stationery sections. A "ding" sound effect is used to emphasize key points. The acoustic environment is clean, suggesting a well-mixed post-production track with minimal real-world noise interference. (4) During the supermarket segment, the speech rate remains fast but articulated. The BGM tempo stays around 120 BPM. Low-level ambient room tone from the store is briefly audible during pauses in speech. Minor plastic rustling sounds occur when picking up snacks. (5) The narration concludes with a persuasive tone regarding the discount coupons. The music maintains its major-key tonality until the very end, where it undergoes a short fade. A final digital chime marks the transition to the closing QR code screen.
